raw_records.duplicate_of_hint: DESIGN CLASSIFICATION IS BORDERLINE - flagging for the central merge rather than deciding it unilaterally. I classified this as observational_study, not interventional_trial, because: the paper carries no registry number and no phase; the authors never call it a trial; it had no control group; and inclisiran was given on clinical indication, not by study assignment ('All participants with high cardiovascular risk and indications for the escalation of lipid-lowering therapy were treated with inclisiran'), with the authors concluding 'Further research including RCTs is needed'. It could defensibly be read as an uncontrolled, open-label, single-arm, prospective before-after interventional study, since the measurement schedule was protocol-driven ('just before the first injection of inclisiran and after three months, just before the second dose'). The two 'study groups' are risk strata within ONE study, not two studies - do not split them.

source_notes:
SCOPE AND METHOD. I read all 8 assigned documents in full (text-extracted from XML/JSON where needed) and scanned each for coagulation analytes with an explicit regex (aPTT, thromboplastin, prothrombin, INR, fibrinogen, D-dimer, thrombin generation, coagul*, bleed*, h(a)emorrhag*, thrombo*, platelet, clotting, anti-Xa) so that "no coagulation endpoint" claims are evidenced rather than assumed. I recorded 29 study records across the 8 sources: 22 interventional_trial, 7 pooled_analysis, 0 observational/case_report/healthy_volunteer_lab. No record was created for a document itself (the three labels and two FDA reviews are regulatory_summary/product_label carriers, not studies), per the brief.

THE 8 SOURCES CARRY FAR FEWER TRIALS THAN THEIR 122 MEASUREMENT ROWS. Unique interventional trials named across my set, after within-set dedup: 19. Only 8 of them are endpoint-evaluable (report a coagulation endpoint): NCT02553889/CS4, NCT04677803 (rondoraptivon pegol type 2B VWD), ATLAS-INH, ATLAS-A/B, ATLAS-OLE, ION-682884-CS3, ION-682884-CS13 (borderline, see below), and ISIS 420915-CS2/NEURO-TTR.

CROSS-SOURCE MERGES THE CENTRAL STEP MUST MAKE.
1. ISIS 420915-CS2 appears TWICE in my set: as "ISIS-420915-CS2 / NEURO-TTR" from COG-S096 (eplontersen review, where it is the external control) and as "Study CS2" from COG-S081 (Tegsedi ClinPharm review, where it is the pivotal trial). Denominators agree exactly (112 inotersen treated, 60 placebo), confirming identity. ONE trial, not two.
2. ATLAS-OLE (NCT03754790) and "Study LTE15174" are the same study under two names inside COG-S026 alone; I already merged them.
3. COG-S038's trial is also reported as the Bethune et al. Blood 2017;130(suppl 1):1116 abstract (its own reference 10) - watch for a duplicate keyed to that abstract.
4. COG-S052's trial is APOLLO but the label never uses the acronym; match on "NCT 01960348" (written with a space in the label).
5. COG-S003 reports only the type 2B VWD cohort of a basket trial registered as NCT04677803 / EUDRA-CT 2020-003807-32; other disease cohorts published under the SAME registration must not be counted as additional trials.

CRITICAL DEDUP HAZARD - THE "CS2" COLLISION. COG-S096 contains BOTH "ION-682884-CS2" (eplontersen, Phase 3 ATTR-CM, ongoing, planned 1,400 subjects) AND "ISIS-420915-CS2" (inotersen, hATTR-PN, the NEURO-TTR pivotal). The review abbreviates both as "CS2"/"CS-2" in running text. COG-S081 independently uses bare "CS2" for the inotersen study. Any merge keyed on the bare token "CS2" will silently fuse two unrelated trials in two different diseases with two different compounds. Match on the full sponsor prefix only.

ENDPOINT-EVALUABILITY JUDGEMENTS I FLAG FOR REVIEW.
- ION-682884-CS13 (COG-S096): scored TRUE, but only on narrative bleeding/thrombotic events (fatal GI haemorrhage, epistaxis, cerebral infarction) that the reviewer ties to dabigatran and platelet counts. Section 7.6.3.6 explicitly states there were no notable laboratory findings for CS13. A stricter reading sets this to FALSE; the headline count then drops from 8 to 7 evaluable trials in my set.
- GATHER1 and GATHER2 (COG-S084): scored FALSE. The Izervay label reports conjunctival haemorrhage (13%/17% vs 9%), retinal haemorrhage (4% vs 3%) and vitreous haemorrhage (<=1%), but these are intravitreal-injection adverse reactions with no coagulation framing anywhere in the record; the label contains no clotting time, fibrinogen, D-dimer, factor activity or anti-Xa. If the project decides any reported haemorrhage counts, both flip to TRUE.
- ISIS 420915-CS2 as seen from COG-S081: scored TRUE on the fatal intracranial haemorrhage plus the explicit exclusion of "consumptive coagulopathies such as disseminated intravascular coagulation". The hard clotting assays (PT/PTT/INR) for this same trial live in COG-S096, so the merged trial is unambiguously evaluable either way.
- Rondoraptivon pegol (COG-S003): platelet count is a co-primary endpoint, but I based evaluability on aPTT and FVIII activity, not the platelet count, per the project rule.

TRUE NEGATIVE CONTROLS CONFIRMED. COG-S054 (givosiran GIVLAARI label): a whole-label regex scan for every coagulation term returned ZERO matches - the label contains no coagulation word at all. COG-S052 (patisiran ONPATTRO label): the only thrombo-stem hit in the entire label is "thrombophlebitis", listed as a sign of infusion-site extravasation, plus "Extravasation" itself; no coagulation analyte anywhere. Both behave as the dataset expects of negative controls.

COG-S054 DOCUMENT MISMATCH - ACTION NEEDED. The source metadata for COG-S054 lists SIX GalNAc-siRNA labels (givosiran, lumasiran, inclisiran, vutrisiran, nedosiran, plozasiran) and six compounds (COG-OLG053, 129, 130, 131, 132, 133), but only ONE document path was supplied: dailymed_givosiran_givlaari_167e663c-....xml. I analysed only the givosiran label, so my records cover COG-OLG053 alone. The lumasiran (OXLUMO), inclisiran (LEQVIO), vutrisiran (AMVUTTRA), nedosiran (RIVFLOZA) and plozasiran (REDEMPLO) labels - and their trials (e.g. ILLUMINATE, ORION, HELIOS-A, PHYOX, PALISADE) - are NOT represented in my output. Five sixths of COG-S054 is unassessed. Either the missing documents must be routed to a worker or the source must be split.

PHASE IS OFTEN UNSTATED. None of the three product labels (COG-S026, COG-S054, COG-S052) and none of the openFDA record (COG-S084) contains the string "phase" at all; I recorded NOT_REPORTED rather than supplying the widely known phase from memory. Likewise no NCT number appears anywhere in either FDA review (COG-S096, COG-S081) - registry IDs for those trials must come from other sources.

THINGS I DELIBERATELY DID NOT TURN INTO STUDY RECORDS.
- Background citations. COG-S038 cites the Buller 2015 NEJM FXI-ASO knee-arthroplasty trial (its reference 9) and the FOXTROT osocimab trial (reference 17) in its introduction and discussion only; COG-S003 cites the BT200 phase 1 healthy-volunteer trial and the ARC1779 study (references 25 and 21). A passing citation is not a report, so none yielded a record. If the central register wants cited-but-not-reported trials, they must be harvested deliberately and flagged as such.
- Analysis artefacts. COG-S081 describes report "420915-CR01: Report on Investigation into Platelet Count Reductions in the Inotersen CS2 Clinical Program" and a population-PK modelling analysis over "202 individuals who were treated with inotersen, across three different studies" (151 patients from CS2 and CS3). Both are analyses of trials already recorded, not studies, and neither has its own participants.
- Quoted labelling. COG-S096 reproduces TEGSEDI prescribing-information text about thrombocytopenia inside the review; that is label text, not a study.
- Unnamed contributing studies. COG-S054's N=111 pooled set exceeds ENVISION's 94, and COG-S052's N=224 exceeds its trial's 148, implying unnamed additional studies in both programmes. I created pooled_analysis records for the pooled sets but invented no study records for the unnamed contributors.

WHY I RECORDED pooled_analysis ROWS AT ALL. Seven of the 29 records are pooled datasets (QFITLIA N=335/286/270; Eplontersen Treated Set CS3+CS13; GIVLAARI N=111; ONPATTRO N=224; IZERVAY N=733; Inotersen Integrated Set N=152; Crooke 2017 2'-MOE database). I included them because a large share of this batch's measurement rows is drawn from them rather than from any single trial - notably the fitusiran thrombotic-event rates and thrombin-generation statement in the Boxed Warning and Sections 5.1/7.1, and the patisiran extravasation/thrombophlebitis datum. Recording them explicitly as NOT-trials is what stops a downstream count from treating "N=335 patients" or "733 patients" as new trials or new participants. Every one of them re-reports participants already counted in the trials above; none may add to a headline total.

SCOPE: 8 assigned sources read end to end from /home/user/oligos/toxicity/coagulopathy/sources/documents/ (read-only; nothing written under /home/user/oligos). 59 study records returned. Headline-relevant arithmetic: the 119 human clinical measurement rows these 8 sources carry resolve to at most 40 distinct actual human trials, of which only 21 records are endpoint-evaluable here — and 5 of the 59 records are documents/pools/pharmacovigilance that yield NO trial at all.

PER SOURCE.

COG-S085 (faers_coag_signal_table.csv) — 57 rows, and ZERO trials. It is a locally computed disproportionality table over spontaneous reports (13 distinct compound labels, 14 coagulation MedDRA PTs, FAERS grand total 20,692,690). Every number in it is a REPORT COUNT, not a participant and not a study. It is the single largest row contributor of my 8 sources (57 of 119 rows, 48%), which is exactly the trap the project lead flagged: if measurement rows were substituted for trials this source alone would inflate the headline by 57. One record, design=spontaneous_reporting. Its reports may also originate from patients enrolled in the trials registered from COG-S024/S077/S078/S100, so its counts must never be added to any trial or participant total.

COG-S024 (Defitelio US PI) — a product_label; the document is not a study. It reports 3 efficacy studies (Study 1 n=102 prospective; Study 2 n=75 prospective/dose-finding; Study 3 n=351 expanded access), 1 pooled safety population (n=176), and 1 dedicated renal-impairment clinical pharmacology study. NO registry number appears anywhere in the SPL (grep for 'NCT' returns 0 hits) and no sponsor protocol codes are used — only the label's own 'Study 1/2/3'. All 22 of this source's measurement rows hang off Table 2 (the n=176 pool) and section 12.2 (Study 2's PAI-1), i.e. off ONE pool plus ONE study, not off three trials. Two cautions: (a) 102+75=177 but the safety population is stated as 176, an unexplained one-patient discrepancy in the label itself; (b) Study 3 is an expanded-access programme that the label explicitly contrasts with 'two prospective clinical trials' — I classified it interventional_trial because the drug is protocol-assigned, but a central ruling may prefer to hold expanded-access protocols out of the headline. NOT RECORDED, deliberately: section 12.2 'Cardiac Electrophysiology' asserts 'At a dose 2.4 times the maximum recommended dose, DEFITELIO does not prolong the QTc interval to any clinically relevant extent' — this implies a thorough QT study but names no design, population or denominator, so I created no record rather than infer one. Section 8.4 also reports 66 pediatric patients across the trials; that is a subgroup of the Study 1/Study 2 pool, not a study.

COG-S006 (PubMed multi-record file) — the metadata says '11 MEDLINE records' but the file contains 12 (grep -c '^PMID:' = 12; the 12th is PMID 24263002, and PMID 22951415 in record 10 is absent from the citation's own PMID list). I registered all 12. This resolves to 6 actual clinical trials (Regado 1a n=85; repeat-dose n=39; phase 1b n=50; NCT00715455 phase 2a n=26; RADAR NCT00932100 n=800 target; REG2 phase 1a n=36), 1 pooled PK/PD modelling re-analysis, and 5 ex-vivo healthy_volunteer_lab studies. Two dedupe points the merge must honour: (1) PMID 21724623 is a PK/PD SUBSTUDY INSIDE RADAR, not a seventh trial — I merged it with RADAR into one record and took NCT00932100 from record 8, because record 1 states no registry ID; (2) the REG1 intravenous phase 1a (PMID 17101847, n=85) and the REG2 subcutaneous phase 1a (PMID 22500821, n=36) both involve pegnivacogin but are different systems and routes and must not be merged. Only 2 of the 12 records carry a registry number (NCT00715455, NCT00932100). The 5 ex-vivo studies collectively touch 104+ named donors (PMID 22632032 alone: 55+11+1+37) — none were dosed, so those donors are not trial participants.

COG-S016 (US 2014/0275214 A1, custirsen) — a patent, not a study. 6 custirsen studies named by sponsor code (OGX-011-01, -02, -03, -04, -11, TV1011-DDI-102), 1 pooled '7 completed studies' safety statement, and 1 third-party study (ISIS 104838 / Sewell 2002) reported with data. NO registry IDs and NO enrolment or analysed denominators anywhere for any of them — every denominator field is NOT_REPORTED, which is a real limitation of this source rather than a gap in my reading. Note the internal inconsistency I flagged: the pooled statement claims 7 completed custirsen studies but the patent individually names only 6 (one of which, OGX-011-11, is ongoing) — do not manufacture the unnamed ones. TV1011-DDI-102 is narrated twice in near-identical wording (Detailed Description and Example 1) — ONE study. NOT RECORDED, deliberately: Examples 2-13 are prophetic protocol designs in the present tense with objectives but no results (not conducted studies), and Examples 14-15 are mouse xenografts (animal). Also not recorded: the bare citations Gleave 2002, Akdim 2010 and Glover 1997, and the reference-list-only Yacyshyn 2002 — the patent reports no findings for them, only for Sewell/ISIS 104838, which is why that one alone got a record.

COG-S077 (Waylivra EU-RMP v3.0) — a regulatory_summary; the document is not a study. It states its own trial count explicitly: 'The volanesorsen clinical development programme includes 9 clinical studies.' I registered all 9 by sponsor protocol (ISIS 304801-CS1, -CS2, -CS4, -CS6, -CS7, -CS13, -CS16, -CS17, -CS19) with full Table 5 denominators, plus 2 pools and 1 third-party registry cohort. NO registry numbers of any kind (no NCT, EudraCT, ISRCTN or JapicCTI in the file) and no trial acronyms. Key merge fact: CS6 == APPROACH in COG-S078. Key non-double-count fact: the RMP reconciles overlap itself — 431 patients treated, 345 on volanesorsen, but only '95 unique FCS patients (patients who received at least one dose of volanesorsen or patients who received placebo only have been counted only once)'; CS7's 68 patients include 14 from CS6 and 3 from CS16. CS19 is the only study excluded from every safety pool. ENDPOINT-EVALUABILITY JUDGEMENT THE MERGE SHOULD REVIEW: I set CS6 and the CS2+CS6+CS16+CS7 pool to true on the strength of discrete BLEEDING preferred terms reported per study under a risk category the RMP defines with the 'Haemorrhages (excluding laboratory terms) (narrow)' SMQ (CS6: epistaxis 5, vaginal haemorrhage 2, injection site haematoma 2, petechiae 4), not on platelet count, which the protocol excludes. The RMP's own causal narrative ties that bleeding to thrombocytopenia rather than to a clotting defect, so a stricter reading of 'a bleeding outcome the source ties to coagulation' would set both to false; I flagged it rather than silently choosing. Separately, an 'international normalised ratio (INR) increased assessed as moderate' AE sits in the Hepatotoxicity module between the CS16 and CS7 paragraphs with NO explicit study attribution — I did NOT use it to make any study endpoint-evaluable. The monkey clotting-time and platelet findings in Module SII are animal work and are excluded.

COG-S078 (Waylivra EPAR Product Information) — a product_label; the document is not a study. 4 studies named (APPROACH/CS6, CS7, CS16, CS2) plus 1 pooled Phase 3 FCS safety dataset. No registry IDs. All 4 are duplicates of COG-S077 records; take denominators for CS16 and CS2 from the RMP, which reports them, rather than from here, which does not. The label is internally inconsistent about APPROACH vs CS6 (its Table 6 header calls the 14 rollover patients 'APPROACH-volanesorsen' while its body text calls them patients 'who had received volanesorsen in Study CS6') and gives the dose as 285 mg where the RMP gives 300 mg. IMPORTANT FOR THE 2 ROWS THIS SOURCE CARRIES: both cited loci (SmPC 4.8 'International normalised ratio increased'; Package Leaflet 'an increase in blood clotting time') attach to the pooled N=87 FCS dataset, which the label introduces only as 'the Phase 3 studies in patients with FCS' and never reconciles to a named study list. I therefore set APPROACH and CS7 to endpoint_evaluable=false in this source and put the true flag on the pool — the opposite assignment would let a pool masquerade as two evaluable trials.

TWO DESIGN CALLS I MADE CONSERVATIVELY AND AM FLAGGING FOR REVIEW. COG-S018 (inclisiran, 24 patients) I classified observational_study rather than interventional_trial: no registry number, no phase, no control group, never self-described as a trial, inclisiran given on clinical indication rather than by study assignment, and the authors conclude that RCTs are still needed. It is defensibly readable as an uncontrolled open-label single-arm before-after interventional study, since the measurement schedule was protocol-driven. I chose the reading that does not inflate the trial count. COG-S021 (volanesorsen, 4 patients + 4 controls) I classified observational_study rather than case_report: self-described cross-sectional study with explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria, a defined recruitment window and a matched control arm, but with n=4 it would also fit 'a small unconsecutive series'. In both studies the two patient groups are strata within ONE study and must not be split into two records.

ONE EVALUABILITY CALL THAT COULD GO EITHER WAY. For inotersen CS2 and CS3 (COG-S080) I set endpoint_evaluable=true on the reported MedDRA SMQ Haemorrhages incidence (40/112 vs 20/60 in CS2; 22.8% in CS3), which is a bleeding outcome. But this review ties those haemorrhages to THROMBOCYTOPENIA and injection-site reactions, not to any coagulation assay, and reports no aPTT, PT, INR, fibrinogen, D-dimer, thrombin generation or antithrombin result for either study - the only INR in the document is inside a single CS3 case narrative (INR>2.5 on dabigatran). Under the project rule that platelet count alone does not confer evaluability, a strict reading of 'a bleeding outcome the source ties to coagulation' would flip both inotersen studies to false on this source. I have documented the exact basis on each record so the project lead can decide; this is the single judgement most likely to move the headline count (by two trials).

JUDGMENT CALL THE MERGE MUST ADJUDICATE - PREKALLIKREIN. Four donidalorsen studies (CS1, CS2, CS5, CS9) are marked endpoint_evaluable=true partly or wholly on plasma prekallikrein (PKK) concentration and plasma proenzyme activation. Prekallikrein is a contact-pathway coagulation factor, and three of the six loci the dataset already cites for COG-S082 are exactly the PKK/PPA paragraphs (PDF p.56-57), so the dataset itself treats these as coagulation measurement rows. But PKK is reported there as the drug's PD target, not as a clotting assay. CS2 and CS5 are independently evaluable anyway (CS2 has extended coagulation and fibrinolytic assays in 22 patients plus bleeding TEAEs; CS5 has PTT, D-Dimer, prothrombin INR and PT plus bleeding TEAEs including a PT-rise case). CS1 and CS9 rest on PKK alone (CS9 also on an explicit null bleeding statement). If the merge rejects PKK as a coagulation endpoint, flip CS1 and CS9 to false; CS2, CS5, CS3 and CS7 stay true.

SECOND JUDGMENT CALL - BLEEDING/THROMBOTIC-ONLY EVALUABILITY. CS3 and CS7 (donidalorsen) and Study 102 (tofersen) have no per-study clotting assay; I marked them true on explicit per-study thrombotic/bleeding statements ("There were no thrombotic event AESIs in studies CS2 or CS3"; "No patient in any of the 4 HAE trials had a platelet related AESI", where the AESI definition is a platelet fall accompanied by major or clinically relevant non-major bleeding; and Study 102's Hemorrhage FMQ 43/139 (30.9%)). The tofersen review explicitly ties hemorrhage analysis to coagulation ("Thrombocytopenia leading to hemorrhage is a potential antisense oligonucleotide class effect; therefore, analyses explored other potential causes of bleeding. There was no clinically significant difference in coagulation parameters or platelet levels"), but makes that tie in the Part C section. Platelet count alone was never used to confer evaluability anywhere in my register.

Ionis uses a CSn protocol series for every programme, so bare "CSn" or "Trial CSn" strings collide across drugs. Within my sources alone: CS1 names three different studies (ISIS 301012-CS1 mipomersen Phase 1 n=36; ISIS 678354-CS1 olezarsen Phase 1; AKCEA-CS1 olezarsen Phase 1 in healthy Japanese). CS2, CS3, CS5, CS6, CS7, CS8 each name two different studies across COG-S088 and COG-S095. The worst pairs are CS3 (ISIS 301012-CS3, a 50-patient mipomersen Phase 2 vs ISIS 678354-CS3/NCT04568434, the 66-patient olezarsen pivotal Phase 3 - and the olezarsen review calls the latter "Trial CS3" 187 times) and CS6 (ISIS 301012-CS6, the 141-patient mipomersen OLE that carries the PT>1.2x result, vs ISIS 678354-CS6/CORE 2, an olezarsen trial that had not started). ANY MERGE KEYED ON THE SHORT FORM WILL FUSE UNRELATED TRIALS ACROSS TWO DIFFERENT DRUGS. ENDPOINT-EVALUABILITY CALLS WORTH REVIEWING. The 6 non-evaluable trials are: all three TEGSEDI studies, the Yacyshyn Gut CS9 Crohn's trial, and both QALSODY studies. The TEGSEDI calls are the only judgement calls in this batch and they are conservative. The one sentence that could be argued the other way, and which I judged NON-qualifying, is in the BOXED WARNING and section 5.2: "Possible complications of nephrotic syndrome can include edema, hypercoagulability with venous or arterial thrombosis, and increased susceptibility to infection" - a stated possible complication of nephrotic syndrome, not an observed coagulation measurement or an outcome the label ties to the drug's coagulation effect. If the project lead rules that a thrombotic-risk statement of this kind qualifies, Study 1 flips to endpoint_evaluable=true and the evaluable count goes from 13 to 14. Flagging explicitly because the dataset's 8 COG-S045 rows are all platelet/thrombocytopenia/REMS rows, so this source contributes thrombocytopenia evidence rather than coagulation-endpoint evidence.

COG-S027 (PMC12824673, ATLAS-OLE, fitusiran). 9 records: ATLAS-OLE (NCT03754790) plus the three phase 3 parent trials (NCT03417102 / NCT03417245 / NCT03549871), the unnamed "phase 1 study" and "phase 1/2 OLE" of the fitusiran programme, the ongoing ATLAS-NEO (NCT05662319, no data), and the two pre-specified pooled analyses. Its Discussion quotes NEURO-TTR (inotersen), ENDEAR, CHERISH, a volanesorsen study and the Goedeker and Szabo cohorts, but only as literature citations and only for platelet counts (which do not confer endpoint evaluability), so no records were created for them.

The widely quoted "10 of 53 (19%) nusinersen subjects had a shift to high aPTT" is NOT a CS2 figure - it pools CS2's scheduled measurements with sporadic measurements from other studies, so any measurement row citing Table 23 maps to the pooled record, not to a trial. CS3B's thrombocytopenia (6/56, 11%) is platelet-only and does not make it evaluable. CS03APK is a 3-patient post-mortem tissue study of patients dosed in CS3A - not a separate dosing trial. COG-S092 (EMA CHMP Spinraza assessment report). 11 records covering the same ten nusinersen studies as COG-S090 plus the population PK analysis - this source is a near-complete DUPLICATE SET of COG-S090 at trial level, and the two must be merged study by study (CS1, CS2, CS10, CS12, CS3A, CS3B, CS4, SM201, CS11, SM202). This source is the one that supplies the acronyms (CS4 = CHERISH, SM201 = CS5 = NURTURE, CS11 = SHINE, SM202 = EMBRACE) and several cleaner denominators (CS3B 121 patients; CS4 126; CS12 47 enrolled and treated; CS10 18 of 28 eligible; CS3A 23 screened / 21 enrolled / 20 dosed; SM201 17 dosed at cut-off versus 20 in the safety narrative). ENDPOINT WARNING: this source reports NO coagulation laboratory data for any study - its coagulation content is entirely a class-level warning ("Thrombocytopenia and coagulation abnormalities ... have been observed after administration of other subcutaneously or intravenously administered antisense oligonucleotides"), an important-potential-risk entry in the RMP, and an SmPC instruction to check platelet count/coagulation before lumbar puncture. I therefore set endpoint_evaluable = false for all 11 records. The single borderline case is SM201, whose safety narrative (the locus the dataset cites at PDF p.87) lists subdural/extradural/spinal haematoma and epidural and subarachnoid haemorrhage - but the report attributes these to the lumbar-puncture procedure, not to coagulation. If the merge accepts the LP-bleeding events plus the "check platelet count/coagulation prior to LP" warning as a coagulation tie, SM201 is the only study in this source that would flip to true.

COG-S069 (pubmed_abstracts_clinical_aso.txt). This document is a BUNDLE of 7 PubMed abstracts, not a single paper; it reports 8 distinct trials because abstract 5 (Kahan 2004) describes a phase I (n=17) and a phase II (n=39) trial under one publication, with the aPTT finding stated once for both. The dataset's assigned source is abstract 1 (Glover 1997, ISIS 2302 phase I, COG-OLG134), whose aPTT sentence matches the cited locus; I recorded the other 7 trials too because the document reports them, flagging each with its own PMID so the merge can attribute them to their own source records if they exist. Two compounds here are outside COG-S069's assigned compound: trecovirsen/GEM 91 (abstract 2) and custirsen (abstract 4). KNOWN CROSS-FILE DUPLICATE: abstract 2 (Séréni 1999, PMID 9987700) is the same trial as the standalone document SERENI1999_GEM91_pmid9987700_abstract.txt in the same corpus - one trial, two documents. 6 of the 8 trials carry an explicit aPTT/PTT finding and are endpoint-evaluable; the 299-patient ISIS 2302-CS9 Crohn's trial (abstract 7) and nothing else lacks one. Enrolment is only quotable for 4 of the 8 (22, 17, 39, 43, 299); phase is stated for only 3.

So: 27 distinct human trials, of which 12 are endpoint-evaluable, carried by my 7 sources and 73 measurement rows. The 9 pooled_analysis records must NEVER be added to a trial count.

THE FOUR DOCUMENTS THAT ARE NOT STUDIES. Three EMA assessment reports (COG-S076 Waylivra, COG-S079 Tegsedi, COG-S099 Rytelo) are regulatory_summary documents and two DailyMed SPLs (COG-S049 Spinraza, COG-S047 Tryngolza) are product_label documents. Per the rule I produced NO record for the documents themselves — only for the trials they describe. If the central merge finds records elsewhere typed regulatory_summary or product_label for these same five source_ids, those are document-level artefacts and should be dropped, not merged as studies.

WHY 749 "CLINICAL" ROWS IS NOT A TRIAL COUNT — CONCRETE EVIDENCE FROM MY SOURCES. (1) One trial generates dozens of rows: fitusiran NCT02554773 alone carries 29 of my 73 rows across six loci. (2) The same trial appears under three names: inotersen CS2 = ISIS 420915-CS2 = NEURO-TTR = EudraCT 2012-001831-30, all in one document. (3) Regulatory reports re-report trials already counted: the Waylivra AR describes 8 volanesorsen trials and the Tegsedi AR 3 inotersen trials, none of which is the document. (4) Pooled sets masquerade as denominators: Waylivra's "N=86" FCS set, Waylivra's "Volanesorsen (N = 108)" phase 3 pool, Tegsedi's "longitudinal safety set" (112), Rytelo's "175 imetelstat" and "391 imetelstat" groups, Spinraza's "385 patients"/"128 patients" exposure sets, and Tryngolza's "1,061 adult patients" — all are participant or pooled counts over trials already counted. (5) One registered trial is split into two table rows: Rytelo's tabular overview lists "63935397MDS3001-Phase 3d" (N=177) and "63935397MDS3001-Phase 2c" (N=57) separately, yet the AR calls it one "Phase 2/3 study (Study MDS3001; IMerge)" under one NCT and one EudraCT. I recorded it as ONE trial; a naive reader would count two.

ENDPOINT-EVALUABILITY CALLS THE MERGE SHOULD KNOW ABOUT. I applied the platelet-alone exclusion strictly, and it changes several verdicts.
- Nusinersen (COG-S049) is the most important case. The Spinraza label's whole coagulation presence — Section 5.1 "Coagulation abnormalities and thrombocytopenia ... have been observed after administration of some antisense oligonucleotides", the Section 2.4 requirement to obtain "Prothrombin time; activated partial thromboplastin time", and the Section 17 counselling text — is an ANTISENSE-CLASS warning and a MONITORING REQUIREMENT. It reports NO aPTT, PT, INR, fibrinogen or D-dimer VALUE for any nusinersen trial. The only per-trial numbers are platelet counts (24 of 146 vs 10 of 72, pooled Study 1 + Study 2; two patients <50,000/microliter in Study 2), which the project rule excludes. Study 2 (NCT02292537) is endpoint_evaluable ONLY because Table 3 reports epistaxis 7% vs 0% — a bleeding adverse reaction that Section 5.1 of the same label ties to coagulation. Studies 1, 3 and 4 are therefore FALSE. If the dataset's 7 Spinraza rows are read as coagulation measurements, 5 of the 7 cited loci (5.1 first sentence, 5.1 paragraph 2, 2.4, Section 17, and arguably Table 3's platelet context) are class warnings, monitoring instructions or platelet data, not trial coagulation endpoints.
- Volanesorsen CS2 is FALSE by a deliberate, narrow call: its only CS2-specific safety data are platelet reductions (Tables 40/41), and the one bleeding figure it feeds ("in the combined phase 2 and 3 studies") does not name CS2. By contrast the olezarsen bleeding statement DOES name its trials ("Across all trials (Trials 1, 2, and 3)"), so Trials 1-3 are TRUE. If the merge prefers a uniform rule, CS2 is the record to revisit; I chose not to infer.
- Fitusiran NCT02035605 (the phase 1 parent) is FALSE: the AT-lowering/TG sentence citing it is a background sentence bundling preclinical data + this phase 1 + three phase 3 trials, with no denominator, arm or value. Another source will have to carry that endpoint.
- Inotersen CS1 and imetelstat MYF2001 are FALSE: CS1 reports only "No consistent effect on platelets"; MYF2001 sits in Group C, which the Rytelo AR explicitly says "is not further discussed in this report".

STRONGEST COAGULATION EVIDENCE IN MY SET, for grading. Imetelstat MDS3001/IMerge is the only trial in my seven sources with named clotting-assay results over time (aPTT and prothrombin INR trajectories in both Phase 3 and Phase 2, plus "Prothrombin time prolonged 1 (0.8%)" and an exposure-adjusted haemorrhage incidence rate). Fitusiran NCT02554773 is the only one with mechanism-level coagulation pharmacodynamics (AT activity and thrombin generation with means and SDs). Trecovirsen GEM 91 is the cleanest single-analyte signal (dose- and concentration-related aPTT prolongation at >=2.0 mg/kg). Inotersen CS2/CS3 report aPTT/INR/PT only as a negative ("did not constitute a safety issue in either study"). Volanesorsen CS6/CS16/CS7 are bleeding-event evidence with one INR row in a pooled table.

DEDUPLICATION HOOKS FOR THE CENTRAL MERGE.
- Fitusiran: NCT02554773 = LTE14762 = "phase 2 OLE". NCT02035605 is its separate parent. ATLAS-INH / ATLAS-A/B / ATLAS-PPX appear ONLY in COG-S028's reference list and are NOT reported as studies there — if they arrive from another source, they are three further trials, not duplicates of mine.
- Volanesorsen: CS6 is almost certainly APPROACH/NCT02211209, CS16 almost certainly COMPASS/NCT02300233, CS7 almost certainly APPROACH-OLE/NCT02658175. None of these registry numbers or acronyms appears anywhere in the Waylivra AR — grep for NCT/EudraCT/ISRCTN returns ZERO hits in that 8,735-line document — so match on sponsor code + population + design + denominators.
- Inotersen: CS2 = NEURO-TTR = EudraCT 2012-001831-30 (no NCT in this document). CS3 is its OLE and shares patients (85 CS2-inotersen + 49 CS2-placebo rollovers = 134) — count separately but do not add 134 to 172 as new participants.
- Imetelstat: MDS3001 = IMerge = NCT02598661 = EudraCT 2015-002874-19, ONE trial. MYF2001 is almost certainly IMbark/NCT02426086.
- Nusinersen: Study 1 = NCT02193074 (ENDEAR), Study 2 = NCT02292537 (CHERISH), Study 3 = NCT02386553 (NURTURE), Study 4 = NCT04089566 (DEVOTE). The label uses no acronyms. Study 4 reuses Study 1 patients as "historic matched sham-control" — shared controls, not new participants.
- Olezarsen: Trial 1 = NCT04568434 (Balance), Trial 2 = NCT05079919 (CORE), Trial 3 = NCT05552326 (ESSENCE). The label uses no acronyms.
- Trecovirsen: no registry ID exists (1999 publication); match on compound + IV route + 0.1-2.5 mg/kg single ascending dose + PMID 9987700.

LOW-CONFIDENCE RECORDS — FLAGGED, NOT DROPPED. Three records have almost no identity and should be resolved from other sources before any headline count treats them as verified trials: (a) volanesorsen CS19 — its only appearance in the entire document is a Table 17 caption, "studies CS1 and CS19", and the AR elsewhere says "A total of 7 clinical studies have been conducted with volanesorsen" while listing 7 others, so CS19 may be a relabelling or sub-part rather than an eighth trial; (b) imetelstat CP14B015 — appears ONLY in the Group C pool list and is ABSENT from the AR's own tabular overview of clinical studies, so that document is internally incomplete about it (it is plausibly the ET/PV study, since Group C's population list names ET and PV but no other listed study covers them); (c) the unnumbered Spinraza "open-label clinical study in infants with symptomatic SMA" that reported severe hyponatremia, plus the label's reference to "open-label clinical trials ... in ... symptomatic SMA" — at least one further nusinersen trial exists beyond Studies 1-4 with no registry ID, denominator or phase.

THINGS I DELIBERATELY DID NOT RECORD AS STUDIES, with reasons.
- Planned/imposed future studies: Waylivra's non-interventional PASS and FCS disease registry ("the applicant should conduct and submit the results of a ... Non-interventional PASS"), Tegsedi's proposed registry study and its two "A non-interventional, multinational," commitments, and Rytelo's "MDS3001 Extension Phase". These report no human data yet; they are commitments, not studies. If the merge wants them, they belong in a separate pipeline column, never in a trial count.
- The Steensma et al. 2021 ex-vivo hTERT analysis in the Rytelo AR: a correlative biomarker sub-analysis of MDS3001 Phase 2 patient samples from patients dosed in vivo. It is NOT a healthy_volunteer_lab (no donated blood from undosed donors) and not a separate trial — it is folded into the MDS3001 record.
- The two rash case narratives and the one hyponatremia narrative in the Spinraza label: individual patient descriptions WITHIN clinical trials already counted, not standalone case reports, and not coagulation-related. Recording them would double-count trial participants as separate studies.
- Subsets that are not studies: inotersen CS2's CM-ECHO subset and its ~20-subject PK subgroup (the latter is the only place "coagulation" assessments are named as collected in CS2); volanesorsen CS2's four groups/three arms; Spinraza Study 4 "Part B".
- No source of mine contains any FAERS or pharmacovigilance case series, so spontaneous_reporting is correctly zero across my seven documents.

DATA-QUALITY WARNINGS ON QUOTED FIGURES. (1) The Waylivra AR's bleeding time-window sentence is internally inconsistent as printed — "44 (30%) <= 13weeks, 16 (12.5%) > 13-26 weeks, and 17 (3.4%) > 26 weeks" cannot share one denominator; I transcribed it exactly as printed rather than correcting it. (2) The Waylivra AR names its FCS pool composition as "the pivotal and support studies (CS7 and CS16)" while CS16 is the sHTG study, so the N=86 FCS pool's membership (which I read as CS6+CS7) is stated inconsistently in-source. (3) The Rytelo AR writes the same sponsor code three ways — 63935397MDS3001, 63935937MDS3001 and MDS3001 — and 63935937MYF2001; I preserved the variants. (4) Several Waylivra and Rytelo denominators exist only inside column-formatted PDF-to-text tables where values land on consecutive lines; I marked every such quote "(column-formatted)" so the merge knows the quote is a faithful line-sequence rather than a running sentence. (5) Spinraza Table 4's Study 4 arm denominators did not survive the XML-to-text extraction, so Study 4's analysed figure is NOT_REPORTED rather than guessed.
